summary.text: Saint Benedict was an Italian monk and abbot whose Rule helped shape Western monastic life. He is commemorated in the Orthodox calendar on March 14.

blocks.text: The OCA places his birth in Nursia in 480. Sent to study in Rome, he chose an ascetic life. A hermit guided him into monasticism, and he lived for a time in a cave at Subiaco.

blocks.text: Disciples gathered around him, and he organized monastic communities with experienced leaders. Opposition accompanied his efforts. He later founded Monte Cassino, which became an important center of learning and manuscript preservation.

blocks.text: The ecclesiastical life dates Saint Benedict’s repose to 547. It does not describe martyrdom. It identifies the second book of Saint Gregory’s Dialogues as the principal narrative source for his life.

blocks.text: His Rule draws on the desert monastic tradition and Saint John Cassian. It organizes common life, work, obedience, formation, and the abbot’s responsibilities. His Orthodox commemoration belongs to the shared history of the first-millennium Church.
